title: Younger adults are sequencing ambition around financial security, sustainable work, purpose, and practical AI capability
source_unit: Deloitte Global, 2026 Gen Z and Millennial Survey: Progress on Their Own Terms
geography: 44 countries; more than 22,500 Gen Z and millennial respondents, with qualitative business-leader interviews

observations.period: 2026; cost of living, housing, life sequencing and career decisions

denominator.unit: more than 22,500 Gen Z and millennial respondents across 44 countries

housing_affects_work_gen_z.unit: percent of Gen Z respondents saying housing availability or affordability directly affects career decisions or where they can work

housing_affects_work_millennials.unit: percent of millennial respondents saying housing availability or affordability directly affects career decisions or where they can work

delay_major_decisions_gen_z.unit: percent of Gen Z respondents delaying major life decisions because of their financial situation

delay_major_decisions_millennials.unit: percent of millennial respondents delaying major life decisions because of their financial situation

cannot_afford_home_gen_z.unit: percent of Gen Z respondents saying they cannot afford to own a house

cannot_afford_home_millennials.unit: percent of millennial respondents saying they cannot afford to own a house

observations.method: Deloitte global survey of Gen Z and millennials across 44 countries, supplemented by qualitative business-leader interviews; the public report compares generational responses and year-over-year measures.
observations.uncertainty: The survey is descriptive and sponsor-produced; reported delays, housing constraints and career choices are associations and self-reports, not causal estimates of housing or inflation effects.
observations.subgroup: Gen Z and millennial respondents across 44 countries, with comparisons by generation, financial condition, work experience and career priorities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Delaying milestones can reflect deliberate sequencing, education or caregiving choices rather than only deprivation; personal financial optimism remains stronger than macroeconomic optimism for many respondents.

observations.period: 2026; leadership, AI adoption, mental health, digital fatigue, purpose and work design

denominator.unit: Deloitte Gen Z and millennial survey frame

rapid_promotion_preference_gen_z.unit: percent preferring rapid promotions and title changes

rapid_promotion_preference_millennials.unit: percent preferring rapid promotions and title changes

ai_use_gen_z.unit: percent reporting some day-to-day work use of AI

ai_use_millennials.unit: percent reporting some day-to-day work use of AI

good_mental_health_gen_z.unit: percent rating mental health good or extremely good, up from 52% in 2025

digital_fatigue_gen_z.unit: percent reporting digital fatigue from alerts and multiple tools/platforms

purpose_important_gen_z.unit: percent saying a sense of purpose at work is important to job satisfaction

observations.method: Cross-sectional global survey with repeated-year comparisons and qualitative leader interviews; measures cover work preferences, AI use, mental health, stress, digital fatigue and purpose.
observations.uncertainty: Year-over-year changes are not necessarily panel changes; mental-health and AI-use measures are self-reported, and the public summary does not establish whether organizational practices caused the reported outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Gen Z and millennial workers, people considering leadership, AI users, respondents reporting stress or digital fatigue, and respondents prioritizing purpose and sustainable workload.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower appetite for rapid promotion does not mean lower ambition: 76% of Gen Z and 67% of millennial respondents report interest in senior or executive leadership over the course of their careers.

related_sources.claim: Canonical Deloitte publication page with sample, findings, and downloadable report.
The survey is the 15th anniversary edition and includes more than 22,500 respondents across 44 countries.

boundary: This record adds a generational work-and-life sequencing route connecting cost of living, housing, major life decisions, sustainable workload, AI adoption, mental health, digital fatigue, purpose and leadership. It is not a causal labor-market model, a representative estimate of all young adults, an employer audit, or respondent-level raw-data ingestion.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Deloitte landing page and 53-page report PDF were reviewed; sample, housing and financial-delay measures, leadership preferences, AI use, mental-health and digital-fatigue measures, and purpose findings were cross-checked.
